name: Humanitarian funding gap
summary: Humanitarian appeals badly underfunded; WFP cut Gaza food aid for 500,000
state: WHO's Sudan health appeal was only 23% funded as of mid-October (WHO, 12 Oct), and WFP cut monthly food aid in Gaza from 1.6 million to 1.1 million people from late October after receiving less than half its usual funding. UNHCR's winter appeal warns resources are dwindling. No new pipeline break was reported as of 4 Nov.
for_you: Aid agencies' appeals are the main route for public support.
rubric_hit: Major ration cuts announced = Watch; no famine-country pipeline break

sources.title: WHO — IPC Sudan alert and appeal funding
UNHCR — Winter appeal as resources dwindle

why: When appeals go unfunded, food aid and health services are cut first; funding gaps lead famine and displacement by months.
drivers: Donor budgets and aid cuts, new crises competing for funds, access constraints.

rubric.alert: Pipeline breaks forcing large-scale suspension of food or health aid in famine-risk countries.
rubric.watch: Funding more than 10 percentage points behind recent years at the same point, or major ration cuts announced.
rubric.normal: UN global appeal funding in line with recent years; no major ration cuts.
